messages:
maria: Quick sync — we need a reproducible apples-to-apples bench for KV/prefix caching before the next release. I sketched a plan below, want quick ack + any gaps.

maria: Goal: measure hit rate, cache warmup time, eviction churn, and correctness under concurrent replay vs synthetic traffic. Also get p50/p95 token latencies and GPU util for same model + sequence settings.

ajay: high level LGTM. Can you list exact workloads + configs? we should lock kernel selection + quantization to avoid confounding.

maria: Yes. Proposed workloads: 
- synthetic: Poisson arrival process with tunable rps and inter-arrival jitter (short prefix variety)
- replay-harness: replay 10M real requests sampled from production traces (preserve original timing and prefixes)
- shard-trace: deterministic replay but grouped by prefix clusters to stress prefix cache hot-sets

maria: For each workload run: set model=redwood-small-v1, seq_len=1024, batch_policy=continuous_batched, max_batch_tokens=4096, kernel_profile=fixed (no adaptive kernel selection), quant=8bit (locked). collect: hit_rate_by_prefix, per-request latency, token latency p50/p95/p99, eviction_rate (/s), avg_KV_size, GPU_mem_util, CPU_sys, and per-worker KV ops/sec.

oliver: +1 on locking kernel selection. Also add a run with kernel_profile=autoselect so we can measure delta (but only after baseline locked runs). That way we can see if autoselect regresses hit-rate/latency.

lin: Warmup plan suggestion: run warmup phase until stable hit rate for 30s window or 100k requests whichever first. Record warmup_time = time to reach 90% of steady-state hit rate for top-1k prefixes.

sara: Concurrency correctness tests: start with single-worker correctness tests (race-free evict/insert), then run 8/16/32 worker concurrency matrices with interleaved reads/writes. Add an assertion harness that replays operations deterministically and verifies final cache contents + per-prefix counters.

ajay: For apples-to-apples latency, we should replay with identical batching behavior. i.e., take replay traces, pass through batching emulator that mimics runtime batching decisions (batch size, timeouts). That ensures same batch composition as production.

maria: Good. I'll add that to the harness. Example bench command we can run on cluster: 

```
# replay harness (deterministic)
bench-run --workload replay --trace s3://prod-traces/2025-11-sample-10m.json \
  --model redwood-small-v1 --seq 1024 --batch-policy continuous_batched \
  --kernel fixed --quant 8 --workers 16 --warmup 100000 --out /tmp/kv-replay-1767
```

lin: For synthetic Poisson: include variable prefix-length distribution (short/medium/long), and synthetic locality knobs (zipf alpha) so we can stress different hit-rate regimes.

maria: Metrics/alerts during run: stream to bench-metrics: hit_rate_per_min, prefix_hit_histogram, eviction_histogram, tail_latency_events (>200ms), incorrect_lookup_count (should be zero).

bench-bot: run 1767123456 started on cluster-kv-perf-3. config: 16 workers, replay=10M, kernel=fixed. ETA ~ 22m.

oliver: Also capture KV cache internal profiling: per-op latencies, lock contention metrics, eviction scan time distribution. Add flamegraph on CPU for worst 1% requests.

sara: For concurrency correctness, capture occasional diffs vs golden replayer. If diff>0 then fail run and dump trace window around mutation.

ajay: We should keep results as a canonical artifact: store (1) raw traces of requests issued to runtime (sanitized), (2) bench config, (3) aggregated metrics, (4) per-prefix sample top-100 list. Put into s3://redwood-bench/kv/1767123456/.

maria: Action items: 
- maria: implement deterministic assertion harness + add warmup detection (ETA today EOD)
- ajay: prepare the replay subset and zipf configs (ETA tomorrow morning)
- oliver: add kernel-fixed gating and cpu flamegraph hook (ETA today)
- lin: add synthetic Poisson generator with prefix-distributions (ETA tomorrow)
- sara: write concurrent correctness smoke tests + golden replayer (ETA EOD)

maria: Anyone object to running the baseline locked-fixed-kernel runs on prod-like nodes tomorrow 9am PT? want to avoid interfering with heavy prod.

oliver: fine from infra side, just coordinate with capacity-schedule.

bench-bot: run 1767123456 completed. summary: steady_hit_rate=0.71, warmup_time=42s, p95_token_latency=12ms, eviction_rate=3.6/s, incorrect_lookup_count=0. artefacts: s3://redwood-bench/kv/1767123456/results.json

maria: Nice. Please upload the aggregated CSVs + top-1k prefix list. We'll compare synthetic vs replay and produce a short summary for the release notes.

ajay: I'll start the apples-to-apples comparison notebook once artifacts are in. We should compute per-prefix delta in latency vs hit-rate and surface top regressors.

lin: One more: let's add a test to randomize worker placement (same rack vs cross-rack) to catch any network-induced eviction anomalies.

sara: yes, add network perturbation toggle to harness.

maria: Thanks everyone — I'll post a short doc with bench configs and links to s3 after I push the harness changes. :thumbsup:
